read_error.what: ⭐ relative_mse = MSE(read, true features) / Var(true features) — identical in form to exp_gen_variance_eq._hard_read_mse, which is where the centroid quantiser's 0.2783 anchor came from, so the two are directly comparable. ⭐ 'oracle_feature_addressed' is the QUANTISER-comparable number (the law eps ~ N^(-2/PR) is about it); 'request_addressed' is the DEPLOYED path, whose error also carries the R8 embedding's own error.

path: request → R8 prototype embedding → nearest STORED ATOMS (per well) → mean → THE frozen decoder → image → THE external classifier

checked.statistic: in-corner shape balanced accuracy on REAL held-out images

prototype_byte_ledger.role: request embedding == the kNN arm's ADDRESSING HEAD; the store's own byte count excludes the CLU addressing head by the same convention

provenance.atoms_are: ⭐ ACTUAL TRAIN DATA POINTS from store_train (the SAME stored set the landscape will use), ⛔ never k-means centres

row_construction_note: ⭐ ``fit``/``val`` are the STRATIFIED cut (chlu.data.gen_rowsplit), the same one exp_gen_baselines gives the rivals, on the same (seed, 32256, 512) — ⛔ no longer pool[:n_fit] / pool[n_fit:] of a SORTED array, under which ``val`` realised 1 floor_hue value against fit's 10 and no tuned configuration was identified. ``pool`` itself is UNCHANGED, so the atoms and the hold-out are what they were. ⚠ The PRIMARY read-error rows are still ``A`` (``eval_a``, excluded from the pool): ``val`` rows sit INSIDE the atom pool, so their read error is optimistic for a reason the split repair does not touch. See ``row_split.balance`` for the realised per-factor counts.

row_split.rule: deficit-priority greedy on the pool's own per-factor marginals (target[f][v] = n_val * count_pool[f][v] / n_pool), seeded tie-break
